categories.name: Cohesión y Coherencia
categories.description: cohesion or discourse-organization error (includes connector misuse, paragraph structure, logical sequencing).
subTypes: Connector-level: missing connector, wrong connector, missing temporal marker, repetitive linking structure.
Discourse-level (most significant at B2 and above): paragraph lacks a clear main idea (no topic sentence), ideas within a paragraph are not logically ordered.

examples.text: Fui al cine. Vi una película.
examples.label: C

examples.text: Fui al mercado y compré fruta. Comí en casa. Después estudié.
examples.note: three clauses juxtaposed without connectors showing sequence or contrast at B1
examples.label: C

examples.text: Hay muchos plásticos en el océano. El reciclaje es costoso. Por eso debemos reciclar más.
examples.note: the paragraph lists facts before stating the main claim, leaving the reader uncertain what point is being made
examples.label: C

categories.name: Gramática
categories.description: verb conjugation, prepositions (selection, not spelling), gender/number agreement, word order, articles. See also: ser/estar distinction (criticalRules).

examples.note: if "el" is wrong gender for the noun
examples.label: G

categories.name: Léxico
categories.description: wrong vocabulary, literal translations from L1, unnatural usage, register mismatch (a structure or expression grammatically correct but inappropriate for the formality level of the task).
subTypes: register mismatch: only flag when the EOI task rubric specifies a register and the mismatch would cost marks (e.g. imperfect subjunctive in an A2 informal letter, highly formal fixed expressions in a casual email). Do not flag slightly elevated vocabulary or register-neutral structures.

examples.note: over-formal for a casual informal letter register when the task rubric penalises register mismatch
examples.rationale: tagged L not G because the register mismatch is the pedagogically salient correction at this level; grammar scope ceiling is enforced separately in the generation pipeline
examples.label: L

examples.note: missing tilde; correct form is música
examples.label: O

criticalRules.preamble: ser/estar (never omit): a verb that violates the ser/estar distinction is always G at every level.
guidance: Use ser for general characteristics, classifications, and cultural norms (es común, es importante, es normal, es difícil).
Use estar for temporary states and ongoing conditions.
If the correct form is a different word (e.g. "esta" corrected to "es"): tag G; spannedText is the verb only; correctedForm is the correct verb.
If only a tilde is missing (e.g. "esta" corrected to "está"): tag O; spannedText is the word only; correctedForm is the accented form.

examples.situation: wrong-word: general state described with estar instead of ser
wrong-word: locative context, estar needed, not a tilde case

antiPatternRules_GUARD: Do not add ser/estar entries here -- it is covered fully in criticalRules above. Adding it would cause duplicate emission in the system prompt.
antiPatternRules: A wrong preposition is G, NEVER L.
A literal translation from the student's L1 is L, NEVER G.
A missing or wrong connector is C, NEVER G.
An ambiguous pronoun or noun-phrase reference where the word is grammatically correct but the referent is unclear is C, NEVER G.
